raw_response:
I will do it close to how I did it before, because on 6.5 mu I cannot gamble. I will keep 4.5 mu in the wheat-maize rotation and 2 mu in cotton. That is what fits my hands, my water, and my money. I watch the fields around me every year, and around here if wheat is hungry in spring or maize is short of fertilizer after the wheat stubble, the yield drops fast and that loss hurts more than spending a bit extra on fertilizer. So I will not cut fertilizer too hard. For wheat, I will use improved seed like most people here, give enough bottom fertilizer, then chase one more nitrogen feeding at jointing, and water two times if the well water is normal. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, because I have seen hybrids fill the ear better than old seed, and I will keep the fertilizer a bit heavier than wheat since maize eats hard in summer. For cotton, I will not plant too much, only 2 mu, because cotton needs more watching, more spraying, and more labor. I will still keep it because if the stand is good it brings cash. I will plough the cotton land, spray it more times than wheat and maize, and water when it sets bolls. I do things this way because it is steady, it matches what has worked on my land, and it does not squeeze the family cash too badly at one time.
